title: Linear changes of coordinates preserve integration
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings) on which $N$ is invertible, and let $d\geq0$. Work in the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the ordinary finite Tate sheaves $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$ and their twists as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space] and let
$$t_{p_d}:Rp_{d!}A_{\mathbf A^d_S}(d)[2d]\longrightarrow A_S$$
be the explicit coordinate-tower counit trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with ordinary etale compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. For every $g\in\operatorname{GL}_d(\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S))$, let $a_g:\mathbf A^d_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_S$ be the $S$-automorphism $v\mapsto gv$. Let $\rho_g$ be its pullback action on $F_S=Rp_{d!}A_{\mathbf A^d_S}(d)[2d]$: use the compact-support exchange [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] for the Cartesian square with both vertical maps $p_d$, bottom map $1_S$ and top map $a_g$, followed by the canonical identification $a_g^*A(d)[2d]\cong A(d)[2d]$. Then
$$t_{p_d}\circ\rho_g=t_{p_d}.$$
Thus every invertible linear change of coordinates preserves this affine-space trace, including $d=0$.

proof.text: Put $G=D(\det)\subset\mathbf A^{d^2}_S$. Over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, its ring is $R[x_{ij},z]/(z\det(x)-1)=R[x_{ij}][1/\det(x)]$; these charts agree on overlaps, giving the open subscheme $G$ and its universal matrix $x$. This algebra is generated by the finitely many $x_{ij}$ and $z$, so $G\to S$ is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; hence $G$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The inverse matrix is $z\operatorname{adj}(x)$, so $v\mapsto xv$ defines an invertible $G$-linear automorphism $a$ of $\mathbf A^d_G$. The matrix $g$ gives a section $s_g:S\to G$ by $x_{ij}\mapsto g_{ij}$ and $z\mapsto\det(g)^{-1}$, and the identity gives $e:S\to G$. These statements include $d=0$, with determinant $1$ and $G=S$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: universal invertible matrix over GL, with the Noetherian hypothesis checked

proof.text: For every Noetherian scheme $T$ over $S$ used below, put $K_T=A_{\mathbf A^d_T}(d)[2d]$ and $F_T=Rp_{d!}K_T$. The input $K_T$ is bounded below. The affine polynomial charts of $\mathbf A^d_T$ and the finite standard affine cover of $\mathbf P^d_T$ show finite type over $T$ [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; hence both schemes are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The projection $p_d$ is separated: over each affine base chart its diagonal is the closed subscheme cut out by $t_i-u_i$. The standard open $\mathbf A^d_T=D_+(T_0)\subset\mathbf P^d_T$ [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], followed by the proper projection [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], compactifies $p_d$. The open is quasi-compact since its intersection with each standard projective affine chart is a principal affine open (or the whole chart). Thus the finite-coefficient exchange theorem [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] applies to these bounded-below inputs, for arbitrary base changes among the Noetherian bases in this argument.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: check the geometric hypotheses for functoriality of compact supports (old split step 2, first part)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] with $f=p_d$ over $G$, $K=K_G$, and the universal linear automorphism $a$ of step 1. The coefficient isomorphism $\theta_a:a^*K_G\xrightarrow{\sim}K_G$ is the canonical ordinary Tate pullback comparison [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The lemma defines the same action as the statement,
$$\rho_a=Rp_{d!}(\theta_a)\circ E_a(K_G),$$
using the Cartesian square $(a,1_G)$, and proves that it is an automorphism. For any Noetherian $u:T\to G$, its base-change equation, followed by the Tate identification of $u'^*K_G$ with $K_T$, gives
$$C_u\circ u^*\rho_a=\rho_{a_T}\circ C_u,\qquad C_u:u^*F_G\xrightarrow{\sim}F_T.$$
The coefficient map in the lemma is exactly $\theta_{a_T}$: the composition compatibility of the canonical Tate comparisons identifies the two pullbacks along $u'a_T=au'$. The identity clause of the lemma and the identity Tate comparison give $\rho_1=1$. The Cartesian-model comparison and its compatibility with changing compactification are part of the cited lemma, not an identification of $a$ with the identity map.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1 and final pullback sentence: action and its base-change compatibility (old split step 2, remaining part)

proof.text:
Write $t_T:F_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$ for the trace isomorphism of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Its base-change formula is $t_T C_u=u^*t_G$. Conjugate the universal action by this specified trace:
$$\alpha=t_G\rho_a t_G^{-1}:A_G[0]\longrightarrow A_G[0].$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], this is the degree-zero image of a unique ordinary $A_G$-module-sheaf automorphism $\alpha_0$. Put $b=\alpha_0(1)\in\Gamma(G,A_G)$. On every etale object and for every section $r$ of $A_G$, module linearity gives $\alpha_0(r)=r\alpha_0(1)=rb|_U$. Thus $\alpha_0$ is multiplication by $b$; applying the same formula to its inverse shows that $b$ is a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], the underlying additive constant sheaf identifies $b$ with a Zariski-locally-constant function $\beta:|G|\to A$. The ring and additive constant-sheaf interpretations agree by their common local constant representatives; the existence of these representatives is also explicitly [lem-weil-pbc-constant-ring-sheaf-sections-locally-constant]. Consequently under any pullback $u:T\to G$ this function becomes $\beta\circ|u|$: pullback preserves each constant representative. Combining the two equations for $C_u$ gives
$$u^*\alpha=t_T\rho_{a_T}t_T^{-1}.$$
This uses full faithfulness only for maps between degree-zero sheaves, never for arbitrary maps in a derived category.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: reduction to multiplication by a locally constant scalar

proof.text: For any field $k$ and any $d\geq0$, the ring $B=k[x_{ij}][1/\det(x)]$ is a nonzero domain. To check this directly, order the finitely many variables lexicographically: the leading monomial of a product of two nonzero polynomials is the product of their leading monomials, with nonzero coefficient. Also $\det(x)\ne0$, since evaluation at the identity matrix is $1$. Inverting its powers preserves nonzeroness and absence of zero divisors: a vanishing product of fractions would give $\det(x)^nfg=0$ in the polynomial ring. In $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $(0)$ is a prime and belongs to every nonempty basic open $D(f)$, since nonemptiness implies $f\ne0$. Every nonempty open contains a basic open and therefore contains $(0)$. Two disjoint nonempty open subsets are impossible, so the spectrum is connected and nonempty. In particular every ordinary residue-field fibre $G_s=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is connected, with the rational identity point $e_s$. These fibres are Noetherian: their rings are the finite-type algebras displayed in step 1 over the Noetherian field $\kappa(s)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: connected fibres; explicit domain and generic-prime argument

proof.text: Restrict $b$ to any $G_s$, writing its corresponding locally constant function as $\beta_s$. The pullback equation of step 4, first along $G_s\to G$ and then along the identity point $e_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to G_s$, identifies the value there with the scalar of $t_{\kappa(s)}\rho_{1}t_{\kappa(s)}^{-1}=1$. Thus $\beta_s(e_s)=1$. A locally constant function on a nonempty connected space is constant [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map], so $\beta_s=1$ on all of $G_s$. This proves the same assertion on every geometric fibre too, but ordinary residue-field fibres already suffice and require no choice of an algebraic closure.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: evaluate at the identity and use connectedness

proof.text: Every point $x\in G$, with image $s\in S$, has a lift to $G_s$: the residue-field map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ and the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to G$ define such a lift by the fibre-product property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since pullback of the function $\beta$ is composition, step 6 implies $\beta(x)=1$ for every $x$. The section/function bijection [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] now gives $b=1$ as a section. Hence $\alpha_0=1$, and the faithful degree-zero inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] gives $\alpha=1$ in the derived category. Unwinding its definition yields $t_G\rho_a=t_G$. If $S$ is empty this same conclusion holds, since the locally constant function on the empty space is unique.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: equality of maps, not merely detection of isomorphisms

proof.text: Finally pull $t_G\rho_a=t_G$ back along the section $s_g:S\to G$. By step 3, $C_{s_g}s_g^*\rho_a=\rho_g C_{s_g}$, since $a$ pulls back to $a_g$. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], $t_S C_{s_g}=s_g^*t_G$. Substitution gives $t_S\rho_g C_{s_g}=t_S C_{s_g}$; cancel the isomorphism $C_{s_g}$ to obtain $t_S\rho_g=t_S$. This is the asserted equality for the specified counit trace. For $d=0$ the automorphism and its action are identities, in agreement with the identity adjunction trace.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, final sentence: pull back along the given matrix
